title: HybridFlow: A Flexible and Efficient RLHF Framework
data_curation: Not a focus of this paper. The evaluation uses the public "Dahoas/ful-hh-rlhf" HuggingFace preference dataset (the Anthropic HH-RLHF split), widely used for LLM alignment; for fair comparison against baselines lacking continuous batching, all generated responses are forced to a fixed length of 1024 tokens (input prompts also 1024), with a global batch of 1024 prompts. No new data sourcing, filtering, or de-duplication is described.
curriculum: Not a focus of this paper. HybridFlow supports the standard PPO-style RLHF 3-stage iteration repeated over training iterations (Stage 1 actor auto-regressive generation, Stage 2 preparation via critic/reference/reward forward passes, Stage 3 actor+critic Adam updates). Experiments use 1 PPO epoch with 8 update iterations per epoch after 10 warm-up iterations, averaged over 5 iterations; no pretrain->SFT->RL staging, self-play, or cross-stage mixing is contributed.
method: HybridFlow is an RLHF *infrastructure* framework whose core contribution is a hierarchical hybrid programming model: a single-controller (built on Ray RPC) coordinates the few-node inter-node dataflow, while each model node runs distributed intra-node computation under the multi-controller paradigm via ParallelWorker classes (3DParallelWorker, FSDPWorker, ZeROWorker). It decouples computation from data resharding through ~8 transfer protocols (collect/distribute functions) and a ResourcePool abstraction enabling flexible colocation/split/standalone placement. A 3D-HybridEngine runs actor training and generation with different 3D parallel configs (p-t-d for training, p_g-t_g-d_g-d for generation) and a novel parallel grouping that achieves zero memory redundancy and minimal all-gather communication during train<->gen resharding. An auto-mapping algorithm (Algorithm 1) enumerates placement plans and parallelism strategies via simulators to minimize per-iteration latency. It supports PPO, ReMax (no critic, extra gen pass), and Safe-RLHF (cost model + pretrain loss) in ~8 lines, integrating Megatron-LM, FSDP, DeepSpeed, and vLLM (with a distributed KVCache manager).
eval_metrics: Metric is RLHF throughput (tokens/sec) = total prompt+response tokens / one iteration time, averaged over 5 iterations after 10 warm-up, on 16 machines/128 A100-80GB GPUs. Compared against DeepSpeed-Chat v0.14.0, OpenRLHF v0.2.5, NeMo-Aligner v0.2.0 across Llama 7B-70B actor/critic/reference/reward models. Headline: 1.53x-20.57x throughput improvement; PPO speedups of 3.67x (up to 7.84x) vs DS-Chat, 3.25x (up to 5.93x) vs OpenRLHF, 12.52x (up to 20.57x) vs NeMo-Aligner; 70B average 9.64x. Transition overhead reduced up to 89.1% (78.2s) over OpenRLHF; transition time cut 55.2% (11.7s) average. Smaller gen TP (t_g=2 for 7B, 4 for 13B) cuts generation latency 60.3%/36.4%. Strong scaling efficiency 66.8%; placement algorithm runtime grows linearly, under 30 min.
key_results: PPO on 7B-70B Llama models: HybridFlow beats DeepSpeed-Chat 3.67x (up to 7.84x), OpenRLHF 3.25x (up to 5.93x), NeMo-Aligner 12.52x (up to 20.57x); overall 1.53x-20.57x across PPO/ReMax/Safe-RLHF. 3D-HybridEngine reduces actor train<->gen transition overhead by up to 89.1% (78.2s) and transition time by 55.2% (11.7s) on average vs OpenRLHF.
evolution_note: Builds on the single-controller dataflow tradition of RLlib/RLlib Flow and the multi-controller efficiency of Megatron-LM/vLLM/DeepSpeed, reacting to the inflexibility and redundancy of first-generation RLHF systems (DeepSpeed-Chat, OpenRLHF, NeMo-Aligner) that hardcoded one placement and resharding scheme. Released as the open-source veRL project, it became a widely adopted substrate that enabled the later 2024-2025 shift from reward-model alignment toward verifiable-reward RL (GRPO/RLVR) for reasoning, by allowing arbitrary reward modules to be plugged in as remote functions.
